1972 Chevrolet Nova Is Anything But Original, Rocks 'Big Shoes' and a Proper Stance For the LSA V8
12 photos
Photo: Garage Kept Motors / Instagram
The Chevrolet Chevy II, aka Chevy Nova , was originally a compact car produced between the 1962 and 1979 model years. It was the inaugural model for the then-new GM X platform, tucked between the Chevrolet Corvair and the beloved Chevelle in the brand’s model line.
From 1969 onward, all versions adopted the famous Chevrolet Nova moniker, and the nameplate went down in history especially because of the success of the third generation among automotive enthusiasts – rooted in the fact that Chevrolet quickly understood the potential of the Nova Super Sport turning from a simple trim option into a veritable performance package and into one of the smallest muscle cars from Detroit.
Nevertheless, the idea was quite popular and led to the arrival of other derivatives like the Rally Nova or the creation of the Yenko Novas by the retired race car driver and muscle car specialist Don Yenko of Yenko Chevrolet in Canonsburg, Pennsylvania, who took the Nova alongside Chevelles and Camaros to modify for extra performance – turning them into weapons against the Ford Mustangs, Plymouth Barracudas and Dodge Challengers of the time.
The special Chevy was even known as the Yenko Supernova, and all these had tremendous impact on enthusiasts, who love the series even today – some more than others, and in many different ways. While many classic car aficionados love keeping them just the same as they were during the moment they went out of the factory gates, the restomod current has gained more and more traction in recent years – mixing the classic looks with modern performance and maneuverability.
This is the case here, as proudly announced by Grand Rapids, Michigan-based Garage Kept Motors : “If the stance and shoes aren't a big enough hint, this '72 Nova is anything but original. Another resto-modded classic muscle car graces our showroom and announced its arrival without subtlety.” The package includes a Nova sourced from a private collection and professionally built by GR Classics.
It’s finished in white over black with black Rally stripes, and this Chevy Nova has less than 2,500 miles recorded on the odometer since it was built. It comes with oversized Rally-style reproduction wheels, and under the hood resides a potent LS3 V8 packing 6.2 liters and an LSA supercharger, delivering both power and “an unforgettable exhaust note” through the Black Widow dual exhaust.
The V8 is paired with a 4L80 automatic transmission equipped with a B&M Slap Shifter; a Holley EFI system with a touchscreen interface provides modern engine management; the “chassis and braking system have been upgraded to match the car's impressive power,” and there’s even push-button start for the mighty V8.
Inside, the classic Chevy Nova cabin has a custom black bucket seat arrangement, a bespoke stereo system with Bluetooth connectivity, Vintage Air conditioning, and custom switchgear to go with the Kenwood audio and the Procar Rally Smoothback buckets. Of course, it ain’t cheap: the asking price is $94,900 – but at least it’s not a six-figure deal.
